newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-ZILE SAYS 2-YR T-BILLS TO HELP MARKET DEVELOP.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-ZILE SAYS 2-YR T-BILLS TO HELP MARKET DEVELOP.

text.p: Finance Minister Robert Zile on Tuesday welcomed a planned first-time issue of two-year Treasury bills, due Wednesday, and said it would help the development of the country's financial markets.
A total 17 million lats of two-year T-bills is planned. The longest issue so far has been one year paper.

"The finance ministry, issuing these two-year securities, is not only fulfilling the government declaration but is also taking a big step for the future development of the Latvian financial market," Zile said in a statement.
He said the issue of the two-year paper will increase the stability of the financial system and allow the state to reduce its issue of short-term paper.
"This is one of the main aims of the issue of these bonds, which will allow us to fulfill our financial plans," he added.

The ministry said some 448.98 million lats of 28-day paper are currently outstanding, some 260.39 million lats of 91-day bills, 178.97 million lats of 182-day paper and 80.43 million lats of 364-day paper has been sold.
